newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish government in newspaper legal action.
newsitem.headline: Turkish government in newspaper legal action.

text.p: The Islamist-led Turkish government is taking legal action against its critics in the top secularist newspapers for breaking a law on giveaway promotions, a minister said on Thursday.
Industry Minister Ali Riza Gonul said his ministry had given a petition to an Istanbul prosecutor alleging coupon schemes run by the Milliyet, Hurriyet and Sabah dailies contravened the law.
He said the two groups who own the papers had appropriated "unjust benefits" from their 1.25 million readers by changing the conditions on their gift promotions months after they began.
"What is important to us is to protect the consumer...We do not have any prejudice against or preference for any group or newspaper," Gonul told a news conference.
The three newspapers have been the target of a steady stream of criticism from the government, which has accused sections of the media of sowing political instability.
The coalition, led by Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, has been crumbling in recent weeks under pressure from the secularist establishment.
